subject: POC scope: multilingual model shortlist, success metrics, and owners
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana@lingopay.com>, Marc Gonzalez <marc.gonzalez@lingopay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-11T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: POC scope: multilingual model shortlist, success metrics, and owners

Hi Ana / Marc —

Thanks again for the demo call this morning. I wanted to capture next steps and propose a concrete POC scope so we can lock timelines:

POC objective
- Validate customer-facing Spanish + French conversational flows (support & billing flows) at production quality and acceptable latency/cost envelope.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Intent accuracy (slot+intent F1) >= 90% on Spanish customer support intents (tiered acceptance: 90% primary, 85% acceptable)
- Human-eval pass rate >= 85% on a 200-sample Spanish test set for helpfulness/accuracy
- p50 response latency < 350ms, p95 < 1s for 99% of production-like traffic
- Cost target: average inference cost below our mutual target (TBD — you mentioned a guidance earlier)

Model shortlist for the POC (open models we recommend trying in this order):
1) LLaMA-2-13B-chat (quantized 8-bit, Redwood-optimized) — primary candidate for quality in Spanish/French
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized) — lower-cost, good instruction-following baseline
3) Falcon-40B-lite (8-bit) — quality/responsiveness tradeoff for complex edge cases
Fallback: distilled 3B variant for low-latency fallbacks (routing on token budget/latency SLO breaches).

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Week 0: data handshake (we receive 1k anonymized transcripts + acceptance rubric)
- Week 1–2: model candidate runs + internal metrics + human eval sampling
- Week 3: customer review, tuning, and acceptance tests

Owners (proposed):
- Customer lead: Ana Ruiz (LingoPay)
- Redwood AE / project owner: Marissa Cole
- Redwood infra/serving: Ben Carter
- Redwood eval & rubric: Priyom Das

Attachments: PoC SOW draft and model-eval-matrix (baseline metrics we’ll track). Please review and flag anything missing.

Would you be able to:
- Confirm the success criteria above (or propose edits)?
- Confirm whether data residency in the EU is a hard requirement for the POC (we can run in eu-central region or use Private deployment if needed)?
- Approve a kickoff week of Jul 24 or Jul 31 (we’ll need signed SOW 72hrs before kickoff for provisioning)?

I’ll loop legal/infra as soon as we get confirmation on residency and timeline.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

Attachment stubs: LingoPay-POC-SOW-Redwood.docx, model-eval-matrix.xlsx

Date: 2028-07-11T12:03:00+02:00
Subject: Re: POC scope: multilingual model shortlist, success metrics, and owners

Marissa — thanks for the recap and clear next steps. A few items from our side:

1) Residency & compliance: EU data residency is required for any logs that include personal data. We will send a redacted SOC2 excerpt — Sara (cc’d) is our legal/procurement lead and will coordinate.
2) Timeline: Jul 31 start is better for us (end of month release constraints). Can you do Jul 31 kickoff?
3) Success metric tweak: for Spanish support, we’re asking that intent+slot recall be prioritized (we can accept slightly lower precision if recall is high). The 90% F1 target is fine as long as recall is >= 92% for key billing intents.

Also looping Sara so she can send the PO/procurement contact. Marc and I will provide 1,000 anonymized transcript snippets by Jul 18.

Thanks — Ana
Ana Ruiz | Head of Product, LingoPay

Thanks — quick technical notes from infra/serving perspective:

- Model recommendations (practical):
  * Primary: LLaMA-2-13B-chat (8-bit quant) — best mix of quality and cost for Spanish/French.
  * Secondary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (intended as a cheaper alternate).
  * Fallback: distilled 3B for strict latency mode.

- Deployment notes:
  * We can host in eu-central-1 (data residency) under Redwood Private or Dedicated depending on SOW.
  * For POC we’ll provision a small dedicated pool with KV prefix caching enabled to improve latency on repeated flows.

- Multilingual eval: please include both automated metrics (intent/slot F1) and a 200-sample human eval per language. BLEU / ROUGE aren’t sufficient; we’ll use a human rubric for factual correctness/helpfulness.

- Owners: I’ll take infra/setup (instance sizing, quantization knobs). Priyom — can you confirm the rubric + labeling plan? Marissa — confirm kickoff date and whether we need a separate legal checklist for residency.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cPoC-eval-matrix (model-eval-matrix.xlsx attached)

Thanks team — attaching the proposed evaluation rubric (inlined below) and a short test plan. High-level:

Evaluation rubric (proposed)
- Acceptance tests (automated): intent F1 (weighted by critical intents), slot recall, confidence calibration check
- Human eval: 200-sample per language; rubric labels: Correctness, Helpfulness, Hallucination (binary), Escalation-appropriateness. Score threshold: 85% pass across samples.
- Performance/ops: latency p50/p95 and outage tolerance (99.9% availability during POC run window).

Test data sources
- Customer-supplied: 1,000 anonymized transcripts (due Jul 18)
- Redwood-synth: 500 synthetic edge-cases for billing flows

Owner & sprint plan
- Week 0 (prep): data ingest, redaction check — Marissa to confirm data transfer method (S3 link vs secure upload).
- Week 1–2: candidate runs + automated metric pass
- Week 3: human eval + customer review

Ask: Marissa — confirm data transfer method and whether Sara will need additional paperwork for the EU residency config.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
